title: QUIZ - 53
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a two-step linear inequality using inverse operations
questions.question: Solve for y: \( 7y + 6 < -36 \)
questions.explanation: Subtract 6 from both sides: 7y < -42. Divide by 7 (positive, so direction is unchanged): y < -6.
questions.hint: Undo addition/subtraction first, then division, keeping track of the inequality direction.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a two-step linear inequality using inverse operations
questions.question: Solve for x: \( 4x - 10 > 22 \)
questions.explanation: Subtract -10 from both sides: 4x > 32. Divide by 4 (positive, so direction is unchanged): x > 8.
questions.hint: Undo addition/subtraction first, then division, keeping track of the inequality direction.

questions.learningObjective: Translate and solve a budget-constrained word problem as an inequality
questions.question: A budget of $87 allows for a $33 fixed cost plus $6 per item y. Write and solve an inequality for the maximum number of items that can be purchased.
questions.explanation: The inequality is \(6y + 33 \leq 87\). Subtracting 33: \(6y \leq 54\). Dividing by 6: \(y \leq 9\).
questions.hint: Set up an inequality where total cost is less than or equal to the budget, then solve for the variable.

questions.learningObjective: Solve a multi-step inequality that requires combining like terms
questions.question: Solve for n: \( 4n + 7n - 6 < -105 \)
questions.explanation: Combine like terms: (4+7)n + -6 < -105. Subtract -6: 11n < -99. Divide by 11: n < -9.
questions.hint: Combine like terms first, then isolate the variable using inverse operations.
